sentences.text: The present appeal has been filed by the claimant in M.C.O.P.No. 258 of 2012 on the file of Motor Accident Claims Tribunal (Sub Court), Kulithalai seeking enhancement of compensation.

entities.text: Motor Accident Claims Tribunal (Sub Court), Kulithalai
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. It is contended by the claimant that the deceased was an agricultural coolie and was aged about 50 years at the time of accident.
He had further contended that his father was earning a sum of Rs.6,000/- per month.
The tribunal after considering the evidence on either side, has fixed the notional income at Rs.4,500/- per month and ultimately, awarded a compensation of Rs.3,17,000/-.
Challenging the said award, the present appeal has been filed.

3. The learned counsel appearing for the appellant relying upon the judgment of the Division Bench of our High Court reported in 2013 (2) TN MAC 450 (M.Sengabagam & others vs. V.Vinod Kumar)
contended that for an accident that has taken place in the year 2008, the Division Bench has fixed the notional income at Rs.6,000/- per month for an agricultural coolie.

entities.text: 2013 (2) TN MAC 450 (M.Sengabagam & others vs. V.Vinod Kumar)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Therefore, the said amount ought to have been fixed https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis by the tribunal.
4. Per contra, the learned counsel appearing for the Insurance Company had contended that the total award amount fixed by the tribunal is reasonable and there is no scope for any enhancement.
5. I have carefully considered the submissions made on either side and perused the material records.

6. As rightly contended by the learned counsel appearing for the claimant, the Hon'ble Division Bench of our High Court in the judgment reported in 2013 (2) TN MAC 450 (M.Sengabagam &
others vs. V.Vinod Kumar) has fixed the notional income at Rs.6,000/- per month for an accident that has taken place in the year 2008 for an agricultural coolie.

entities.text:
2013 (2) TN MAC 450 (M.Sengabagam &
others vs. V.Vinod Kumar)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Considering the above said facts, this Court is inclined to enhance the notional income from Rs.4,500/- to Rs.6,000/- per month.
Considering the age and his self employment, 10% is added towards future prospects.
Therefore, the total monthly income would be Rs. 6,600/-.
Considering the fact that the claimant has left one legal heir, 1/3 is deducted towards personal expenses.
Therefore, the monthly income https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis could be fixed at Rs.4,400/-.

Considering the age of the claimant,
the correct multiplier is 11.
7.
In view of the above said facts, the award amount is re-
assessed as follows:

Loss of income 4,400x12x11 : Rs.5,80,800/- Loss of love and affection : Rs. 40,000/-
 Loss of estate : Rs. 15,000/-
 Funeral expenses : Rs. 15,000/-
 Total : Rs.6,50,800/-
J.Dominic Anthony vs M.Subramani on 14 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/169911173/
2 8.

The award of the tribunal is enhanced from Rs.3,17,000/-
(Rupees Three Lakh and Seventeen Thousand only) to Rs.6,50,800/- (Rupees Six Lakh Fifty Thousand and Eight Hundred only).
The award amount shall carry interest at the rate of 7.5% from the date of filing of the claim petition.
The Insurance Company is directed to deposit the balance amount within a period of eight (8) weeks from the date of receipt of copy of this order.
On such deposit, the claimant is entitled to withdraw the said amount.
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis 9.
With the said observations, this Civil Miscellaneous Appeal stands partly allowed.
No costs.
